title: Functorial countable horn completion and its weak homotopy comparison
statement: Use small simplicial sets, horns, Kan complexes and weak homotopy equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], in a containing universe. For each small simplicial set $K$, form $K_0=K$ and $K_{n+1}$ by attaching, simultaneously, a copy of $\Delta^m$ along every map $\Lambda_i^m\to K_n$ for $m\geq1$ and $0\leq i\leq m$, and set $K^{\mathrm{horn}}=\operatorname{colim}_{n<\omega}K_n$, with colimits computed degreewise in sets. This construction is functorial in $K$. The natural map $K\hookrightarrow K^{\mathrm{horn}}$ is a monomorphism, a Kan anodyne extension, and a weak homotopy equivalence, and $K^{\mathrm{horn}}$ is a small Kan complex. Here Kan anodyne means belonging to the closure of all positive-dimensional horn inclusions under isomorphisms, pushouts, small transfinite compositions and retracts. No vertices are added from a dimension-zero horn: the construction sends the empty simplicial set to itself.

source.place: Proposition 2.1.9 and construction 2.4.36 (small-object horn attachment); Section 3.1 (Kan anodyne extensions and weak homotopy equivalences). Online PDF read on 2026-10-17; local archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text: For each degree $r$, form $K_{n+1,r}$ as the quotient of the disjoint union of $K_{n,r}$ and one copy of $\Delta^m_r$ for each triple $(m,i,\alpha)$ with $m\geq1$ and $\alpha:\Lambda_i^m\to K_n$, identifying the horn elements with their images under $\alpha$. Simplicial operators on these summands respect the relations because $\alpha$ is simplicial, so they descend to the quotient and satisfy the simplicial identities. The quotient has the pushout universal property: a map out of it is exactly a family of maps out of the summands agreeing on the identified horn elements. The same degreewise construction gives the sequential colimit. For $f:K\to L$, postcomposition sends $(m,i,\alpha)$ to $(m,i,f_n\alpha)$; the identity map on the corresponding simplex summand and $f_n$ on the old stage induce $f_{n+1}$. These maps commute with stage inclusions. Postcomposition preserves identities and composites on each summand, hence also on the quotients and their colimits. The stage inclusions and $K\to K^{\mathrm{horn}}$ are consequently natural. The simplex and horn formulas are those of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Paragraph 2, derived coefficient adjunction: agent reconstruction of the inherited horn-completion localization infrastructure. External source read online: Cisinski, Construction 2.4.36 (printed pp. 64–65)

proof.text: A horn is a simplicial subset of its simplex by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], so each horn inclusion into its simplex is injective in every degree. In a pushout of sets along an injection, the quotient identifies each element of the attaching subset only with its specified image in the old set: two distinct old elements cannot be identified. Thus $K_{n,r}\to K_{n+1,r}$ is injective. In the sequential colimit, two old elements are equal only if their images agree at a common later stage, and injectivity there makes them equal already. Consequently $K\to K^{\mathrm{horn}}$ is degreewise injective and is a monomorphism, since equality after postcomposition can be cancelled in every degree. At every stage the attaching maps form a set: they are a subset of the product, over the countably many degrees, of sets of functions. The horn types are indexed by a countable set of pairs $(m,i)$. The fixed containing universe is closed under these products, small disjoint unions, quotients and countable unions, so every stage and the final simplicial set are small in it.

source.place: Paragraph 2, derived coefficient adjunction: agent reconstruction of the inherited horn-completion localization infrastructure. External source read online: Cisinski, Construction 2.4.36 (printed pp. 64–65)

proof.text: Fix $m\geq1$, $0\leq i\leq m$, and $\alpha:\Lambda_i^m\to K^{\mathrm{horn}}$. By the horn formula of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], this horn is the union of its $m$ faces indexed by $j\ne i$. Each such face is generated by the simplex $[m-1]\hookrightarrow[m]$ omitting $j$: every simplex of that face is its restriction along a weakly increasing map. Choose a stage for the image of each of these finitely many generators and take the maximum $n$. Naturality then puts the image of every horn simplex in $K_n$. Because $K_n\to K^{\mathrm{horn}}$ is degreewise injective by the preceding step, the restrictions agree on all overlapping faces already in $K_n$, and the lifted map is simplicial. This gives $\alpha_n:\Lambda_i^m\to K_n$. The copy of $\Delta^m$ indexed by $(m,i,\alpha_n)$ in $K_{n+1}$ supplies the required extension of $\alpha$ into $K^{\mathrm{horn}}$. This works for both outer horns as well as inner horns and for $m=1$, so the Kan condition stated in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] holds.

source.place: Paragraph 2, derived coefficient adjunction: agent reconstruction of the inherited horn-completion localization infrastructure. External source read online: Cisinski, Construction 2.4.36 (printed pp. 64–65)

proof.text: The closure in the statement contains any small coproduct of horn inclusions even though coproducts were not listed separately. Well-order the set of summands, start with the coproduct of all horn domains, and replace one domain at a time by its simplex, keeping the other summands fixed. Each successor map is a pushout of that single horn inclusion, and at a limit take the degreewise union of the preceding stages. The final map is precisely the coproduct inclusion. Thus each $K_n\to K_{n+1}$, being its pushout, belongs to the stated closure. The countable transfinite composite is $K\to K^{\mathrm{horn}}$, so it is Kan anodyne. The same description shows that this map is a transfinite composite of pushouts of coproducts of horn inclusions.

source.place: Paragraph 2, derived coefficient adjunction: agent reconstruction of the inherited horn-completion localization infrastructure. External source read online: Cisinski, Construction 2.4.36 (printed pp. 64–65)

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core] to the map constructed in the preceding step. Its statement identifies trivial cofibrations with retracts of transfinite composites of pushouts of coproducts of positive-dimensional horn inclusions. Our map is such a composite, hence is its own retract and is a trivial cofibration. In the stated model structure this means it is both a cofibration and a weak homotopy equivalence. The core theorem specifies weak homotopy equivalence using geometric realization, components and all based homotopy groups, exactly the convention of the item. This proves the weak homotopy comparison for every $K$, without assuming $K$ was Kan.

source.place: Paragraph 2, localization infrastructure; existing Kan–Quillen core theorem. External comparison: Cisinski, Theorem 3.1.8 and Theorem 3.1.29.

proof.text: *Step 6 (the empty simplicial set).* If $K=\varnothing$, every positive-dimensional horn has a vertex and therefore admits no map to $K_n=\varnothing$. No cell is attached at any stage, so $K_n=\varnothing$ for all $n$ and $K^{\mathrm{horn}}=\varnothing$.
